'''Jeremy Deshawn Evans''' (born October 24, 1987) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Mykonos B.C.|Mykonos]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]] before being drafted by the [[Utah Jazz]] in [[2010 NBA draft|2010]]. During his career, Evans has spent time with the Jazz, the [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Atlanta Hawks]], and [[BC Khimki|Khimki Moscow]] in Russia. In 2012, he was named the NBA Slam Dunk Contest champion.

==High school career==
Evans attended [[Crossett High School (Crossett, Arkansas)|Crossett High School]], where he helped the Eagles reach the state tournament each of his last two seasons. As a junior, he was named All-State, All-League, and was voted the County Player of the Year after Crossett High finished 17–10. As a senior, he averaged 25.6 points, 11.0 rebounds, and 4.0 blocks per game, earning All-State and All-Conference accolades.<ref name="Mavs bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/team/roster/jeremy_evans/ |title=Jeremy Evans bio |work=Mavs.com |access-date=December 11, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151212021633/http://www.mavs.com/team/roster/jeremy_evans/ |archive-date=December 12, 2015 }}</ref>

==College career==
Evans played in college for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]]. As a senior, he averaged 10.0 ppg with a field goal percentage of .639. He is the Hilltoppers all-time leader in blocks with 224<ref>{{cite web|first=Jody|last=Genessy|url=https://www.deseret.com/2010/10/4/20144831/utah-jazz-second-round-pick-jeremy-evans-stands-out-with-athleticism-and-hoops-iq/|title=Utah Jazz: Second-round pick Jeremy Evans stands out with athleticism and hoops IQ|work=DeseretNews.com|date=October 3, 2010|access-date=November 23, 2013}}</ref> and also a member of WKU's 1,000-point club with 1,065 career points, and he wrapped up his career with a 7.9 point-per game scoring average and an average of 5.9 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wkusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102210aaa.html|title=Jeremy Evans Makes Utah Jazz Roster|work=WKUSports.com|date=October 22, 2010|access-date=December 11, 2015|archive-date=April 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414065607/http://www.wkusports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102210aaa.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Utah Jazz (2010–2015)===
[[File:Jeremy Evans Jazz.JPG|thumb|left|Evans with the Jazz in 2014]]
Evans was drafted by the Utah Jazz with the 55th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. On March 4, 2011, he was assigned to the [[Delaware 87ers|Utah Flash]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4161842|title=Utah Jazz Assign Jeremy Evans to NBA D-League Affiliate Utah Flash|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 4, 2011|access-date=December 11, 2015}}</ref> He was recalled on March 6.<ref name=realgm>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jeremy-Evans/Summary/10165|title=Jeremy Evans Player Profile – RealGM|work=RealGM.com|access-date=December 11, 2015}}</ref>

On February 22, 2012, Evans was announced as a competitor in the 2012 [[Sprite (soft drink)|Sprite]] [[NBA All-Star Weekend Slam Dunk Contest]], replacing the injured [[Iman Shumpert]] of the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ian|last=Begley|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/7602339/new-york-knicks-guard-iman-shumpert-dunk-contest|title=Iman Shumpert out of dunk contest|work=ESPN.com|date=February 23, 2012|access-date=February 23, 2012}}</ref> He dunked two basketballs in one dunk over teammate [[Gordon Hayward]] and won the contest with 29% of the votes.

On July 11, 2012, Evans re-signed with the [[Utah Jazz]] to a multi-year deal.<ref name="realgm" />

On February 16, 2013, Evans participated in another Slam Dunk Contest. In one of his dunks, he jumped over a painting of himself dunking, which he himself painted. He went on to lose to [[Terrence Ross]].

===Dallas Mavericks (2015–2016)===
On July 31, 2015, Evans signed a two-year deal with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-forward-jeremy-evans/|title=Mavericks sign forward Jeremy Evans|work=mavs.com|date=July 31, 2015|access-date=July 31, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Mavericks in the team's season opener against the Phoenix Suns on October 28, recording 7 points and 6 rebounds in a 111–95 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/DALPHX/gameinfo.html|title=8 Dallas players reach double figures, Mavs rout Suns 111-95|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330130800/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/DALPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 30, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> During his first year as a member of Mavericks, he had multiple assignments to the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2015-16 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 21, 2016|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 17, 2016, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after undergoing arthroscopic surgery to repair a torn labrum in his right shoulder.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=19104|title=Jeremy Evans undergoes season-ending shoulder surgery|work=InsideHoops.com|date=March 17, 2016|access-date=March 17, 2016}}</ref>

On July 7, 2016, Evans was traded, along with cash considerations and the rights to [[Emir Preldžić]], to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for the rights to [[Stanko Barać]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-acquire-jeremy-evans|title=Pacers Acquire Jeremy Evans in Trade with Dallas|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2016|access-date=July 7, 2016}}</ref> On October 23, 2016, he was waived by the Pacers after appearing in two preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-jeremy-evans-and-julyan-stone|title=Pacers Waive Jeremy Evans and Julyan Stone|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2016|access-date=October 23, 2016}}</ref>

===Khimki (2016–2017)===
On October 29, 2016, Evans signed with Russian club [[BC Khimki]] for the rest of the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.bckhimki.ru/news/clubnews/2016/october/1146/|title=JEREMY EVANS SIGNS WITH BC KHIMKI|work=BCKhimki.ru|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref>

===Erie BayHawks (2017–2018)===
On September 21, 2017, Evans signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Hawks Sign Jeremy Evans and Jordan Mathews|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-jeremy-evans-and-jordan-mathews|access-date=September 21, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=September 21, 2017}}</ref> He was released on October 13 as one of the team's final preseason roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Waive Cavanaugh, Cook and Evans|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-waive-cavanaugh-cook-and-evans?cid=hawks_17releases_w_h_hp_mnb_-_1013_cavanaughcookevanswaived|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 14, 2017|date=October 13, 2017}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2018)===
On April 1, 2018, the [[Atlanta Hawks]] announced that they had signed Evans to a 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hawks Sign Jeremy Evans To 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-jeremy-evans-10-day-contract|date=April 1, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 1, 2018}}</ref>

===Darüşşafaka (2018–2019)===
On August 21, 2018, Evans signed a one-year deal with [[Darüşşafaka S.K.|Darüşşafaka]] of the Turkish [[Basketball Super League|BSL]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/286237/darussafaka-signs-jeremy-evans.html|title=Darussafaka signs Jeremy Evans|access-date=August 21, 2018|work=Sportando.basketball|date=August 21, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Second stint with Khimki (2019–2020)===
On July 25, 2019, [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] announced that they had brought back Evans.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.bckhimki.com/news/clubnews/2019/july/1444/|title=KHIMKI MOSCOW REGION, JEREMY EVANS REUNITE TILL 2020|date=July 25, 2019|work=bckhimki.com|access-date=July 25, 2019}}</ref>

=== Olimpia Milano (2021)===
On February 24, 2021, Evans signed with [[Olimpia Milano]], competing only in [[EuroLeague]] games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Down the EuroLeague regular season stretch, Olimpia will be able to count on Jeremy Evans |url=http://www.olimpiamilano.com/en/down-the-euroleague-regular-season-stretch-olimpia-will-be-able-to-count-on-jeremy-evans/ |publisher=olimpiamilano.com |date=24 February 2021 }}</ref> He parted ways with the team on May 31.<ref>{{cite news |title=Olimpia Milano, Jeremy Evans part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/olimpia-milano-jeremy-evans-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 23, 2021 |date=May 31, 2021}}</ref>

===Panathinaikos (2021–2022)===
On August 21, 2021, Evans signed with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]], penning a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Panathinaikos officially signs Jeremy Evans |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/panathinaikos-officially-signs-jeremy-evans/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 21, 2021 |date=August 21, 2021}}</ref> In 28 [[Greek Basket League]] games, he averaged 6.8 points, 4.3 rebounds and 0.7 blocks, playing around 17 minutes per contest. Additionally, in 32 [[EuroLeague]] games, he averaged 5.5 points, 3 rebounds and 0.5 blocks, playing around 16 minutes per contest.

===Paris Basketball (2022–2023)===
On October 18, 2022, Evans signed with French club [[Paris Basketball]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://parisbasketball.paris/2022/10/jeremy-evans-rejoint-leffectif-parisien/|title=Jeremy Evans Rejoint L'effectif Parisien|last=|first=|date=October 18, 2022|website=parisbasketball.paris|publisher=|language=fr|access-date=October 23, 2022}}</ref>

=== Manama (2023) ===
Evans played for Bahraini club [[Manama Club (basketball)|Manama Club]] in 2023, and won the inaugural [[West Asia Super League]] (WASL) with the team. He averaged 8.3 points per game in the WASL season.

== The Basketball Tournament ==
In 2017, Evans played for the Kentucky Kings of [[The Basketball Tournament]]. Evans averaged 21.5 PPG and 13.0 RPG to help his team advance to the second round of the tournament. The Basketball Tournament is an annual $2 million winner-take-all tournament broadcast on ESPN.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetournament.com/players/jeremy-evans|title=Jeremy Evans|access-date=March 13, 2018|archive-date=November 4, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211104024133/https://thetournament.com/players/jeremy-evans/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In TBT 2018, he played for Eberlein Drive. Eberlein Drive made it to the championship game, where they lost to Overseas Elite. Jeremy also saw stints in TBT in 2021 with Eberlein Drive.

==Personal life==
The son of Gwyn, he has one younger brother, Justin, and is married to Korrie. An accomplished artist, Evans had a sketch of CBS analyst [[Dan Bonner]] showcased on national television broadcast of the Hilltoppers’ second round battle with Gonzaga during the 2009 NCAA Tournament and some of his art was also displayed throughout the WKU athletic offices. He majored in interdisciplinary studies with a concentration in art.<ref name ="Mavs bio" />
